1. AiRA — every question about your work at AiRA

open this topic alone → · 561 questions

1.1 "Tell me about AiRA" — the pitch, your role, the timeline

Learn: DHANESH_AIRA_CONTRIBUTIONS.md "Executive summary" + "Timeline by month" · career/resume.tex (AiRA bullets) · techinterviewhandbook.org/behavioral-interview/

  • L1 Tell me about AiRA in two sentences. Who is the user and what problem does it solve?
  • L1 What was your title and what did "founding engineer" mean in practice day to day?
  • L1 Is AiRA live? Which platforms, how many users, and is it beta or GA?
    beta on iOS and Android; know honest user numbers or say you don't track them
  • L2 The product pivoted several times. Walk me through the phases and what drove each change.
    web chat → WhatsApp assistant → mobile live mode → Omni → persistent personal agent
  • L2 What did you build first when you joined in July/August 2025, and what are you working on now?
  • L2 Pick the one system you are proudest of and explain why that one.
  • L2 Pick the one system you would delete if you could, and why.
  • L2 What is the hardest technical problem you solved at AiRA? Go deep on one.
  • L2 What does a typical week look like for you: coding vs reviewing vs design vs talking to the CEO?
  • L2 How many of your ~1,500 aira-api commits were features vs merges vs fixes? Why so many merges?
    ~400 merges; integration during v3 rewrite; stacked PR branches
  • L3 You list memory, voice, browser agent, reminders and video. That is a lot for one person in 15 months. How?
  • L3 Several systems you built were later deleted (live mode, activities, Ask/Posts, speaker ID). Was that wasted work?
  • L3 If AiRA shut down tomorrow, which of your work would you reuse at your next job and why?

Follow-up chain

  • L2 "Voice-first AI assistant" — what fraction of real usage was voice vs typed text?
  • L2 What metric did the company use to decide a feature worked? Did you ever see it move?
  • L3 Who are your competitors (ChatGPT voice, Gemini Live, Pi) and what can AiRA do that they cannot?

1.2 Architecture end to end

Learn: DHANESH_AIRA_CONTRIBUTIONS.md "Feature index" · AIE ch10 "AI Engineering Architecture" (pdf p473–489) · DDIA ch1 "Thinking About Data Systems" (pdf p24–26)

  • L1 Draw AiRA's backend in boxes: clients, API, workers, queues, databases, LLM providers, external APIs.
  • L1 Which datastores does AiRA use and what lives in each?
    Mongo source of truth; Redis hot state/locks; Qdrant vectors; Memgraph graph; Azure Blob files
  • L1 Monolith or microservices? How many deployable services were there?
    one FastAPI aira-api; separate aira-api-bg consolidation service; relay
  • L2 Walk me through one Omni voice turn, from the phone's mic to audio coming back.
  • L2 Walk me through one typed chat message in the 2025 WhatsApp era, from webhook to reply.
  • L2 What is the "v3 / MACH" layout (controllers, services, entities, adapters) and why did the team move to it?
  • L2 What runs inside the request path and what runs in the background? How do you decide?
  • L2 What state does one API worker hold in memory that another worker cannot see?
    user's WS socket, STT socket, cancel sets, data-key cache
  • L2 What happens when Redis is down? When Qdrant is down? When Mongo is down?
    Qdrant: API boots with vector features off; know the others honestly
  • L2 Where are secrets kept, and how does the app read them at boot?
    Azure Key Vault-backed Secrets settings; features off until secret exists
  • L3 What is the single point of failure in this architecture today?
  • L3 Where is the bottleneck: LLM latency, Redis, Mongo, or the WebSocket workers? How do you know?
  • L3 If you redrew it from scratch with what you know now, what boxes would change?

Follow-up chain

  • L2 Why does the API need both Redis and Mongo for the same data (e.g. short-term memory)?
  • L2 What is per-user state vs per-session state vs per-turn state in your design?
  • L3 How would you split this monolith if the team grew to 20 engineers? Where are the seams?

1.3 Stack choices and trade-offs

Learn: DDIA ch2 "Relational vs. document databases today" (pdf p60–64) · DDIA ch2 "Graph-like Data Models" (pdf p70–84) · qdrant.tech/documentation/ · memgraph.com/docs

  • L1 Why Python and FastAPI for the backend instead of Node/NestJS, which you used at Jigsaw?
  • L1 Why MongoDB over PostgreSQL for the main store?
  • L2 Why Qdrant over pgvector, Pinecone or Weaviate?
    payload filters/indexes, named vectors, self-host; know the trade-off honestly
  • L2 Why Memgraph over Neo4j? Why a graph database at all?
    Cypher, Bolt driver compatible, in-memory speed; user-scoped traversals
  • L2 Why Redis for queues, locks, pub/sub and short-term memory instead of Kafka or RabbitMQ?
  • L2 Why Azure (Blob, Key Vault) and not AWS or GCP?
  • L2 Why APScheduler inside the API instead of Celery beat or a cloud scheduler?
  • L2 Why OpenRouter in front of model providers? What does it cost you?
    one key, many models, fallbacks; extra hop, less control over caching
  • L2 Why Cartesia for TTS and STT? Why did Deepgram get dropped?
    one vendor for both; no reconnect on mode toggle; fewer secrets
  • L2 Why FastEmbed / local 384-d embeddings in places instead of an embedding API?
  • L2 Why Browserbase + Stagehand instead of running your own headless Chrome fleet?
  • L3 Mongo has no joins. Show me a query where that hurt and how you worked around it.
    $lookup aggregation replacing N-per-user count queries
  • L3 You run five datastores with a small team. Was that over-engineering? What would you cut?
  • L3 FastAPI is async. Where did sync code block the event loop and how did you find it?
    sync OpenAI/Exa clients inside async methods
  • L3 Python GIL: did CPU work (Resemblyzer, Pillow/numpy) ever hurt latency? What did you do?
    asyncio.to_thread; later removed torch dependency entirely

1.4 The realtime channel: SSE → Redis Streams → Pub/Sub → WebSocket

Learn: bullets.md § aira-api_s5 item 1 · DHANESH_AIRA_CONTRIBUTIONS.md s5 feature 8 · redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ · html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html · DDIA ch11 "Messaging systems" (pdf p449–451)

  • L1 What does the realtime channel carry?
    reply text, thinking, audio chunks, canvas updates, task events
  • L1 SSE vs WebSocket vs long polling: one-line difference each.
  • L2 Version 1 was SSE plus a Redis Stream per user. How did replay on reconnect work?
    XADD per user, event id = stream id, Last-Event-ID, cursor key
  • L2 Why the 15-second : ping comment on the SSE connection?
    proxies close idle connections
  • L2 A user's event is produced on worker A but their SSE connection is on worker B. How did it reach them?
    one Redis SUBSCRIBE per instance wakes the right local queue
  • L2 Why does a subscribed Redis connection need to be separate from the normal client?
  • L2 Version 2 dropped the Stream and sent the whole payload over Pub/Sub. What did you gain and what did you lose?
    faster, simpler; events while disconnected are lost
  • L2 Version 3 moved to WebSocket. What forced it?
    phone must send audio and commands up, not only receive
  • L2 How did you make the same auth dependency work for HTTP and WebSocket routes?
    retyped Request to Starlette HTTPConnection
  • L2 Native mobile WebSocket clients cannot set cookies. How did auth work then?
    Authorization: Bearer header accepted on the WS route
  • L2 One user, two devices or tabs. How does the server fan out to both?
    routing map holds a set of sockets per user
  • L3 Was dropping durable replay a mistake? What does the user see if they lose signal for 10 s mid-reply?
  • L3 Redis Streams vs Kafka for this exact use case: argue for each.
  • L3 How would you add exactly-once-ish delivery of events to the app today?
  • L3 What exactly did you build here vs your two teammates?
    mine: SSE, Streams replay, Pub/Sub, WS transport; teammates: routing service, TTS payloads

Follow-up chain

  • L2 "What broke at each step?" — name one concrete problem that made you leave SSE, then Streams.
  • L2 How did you trim the stream so Redis memory did not grow forever?
    approximate XTRIM to ~1,000 entries
  • L3 With Pub/Sub, a worker restarts and misses a message. How would you detect and repair that?

1.5 Omni: realtime voice over a single WebSocket

Learn: bullets.md § aira-api_s7 ("Omni") + § aira-api_s6 (inbound event bus, Deepgram) · DHANESH_AIRA_CONTRIBUTIONS.md slice 7 feature 1 · AIE ch9 "Inference Performance Metrics" (pdf p436–443) · docs.cartesia.ai · docs.pipecat.ai

  • L1 What is Omni and what three things did it replace?
    live mode, chat and onboarding pipelines
  • L1 What are VAD, STT, endpointing and TTS? Where does each run in Omni?
  • L1 Why one WebSocket instead of separate STT and TTS connections from the phone?
  • L2 How is audio framed on the socket?
    binary frames with a 1-byte channel id; replaced 4-byte length + JSON header
  • L2 What is the inbound event bus? When does a command go to the Redis queue vs run on the same worker?
    BLPOP queue load-balances LLM turns; session commands stay with socket owner
  • L2 What does the pipeline load before calling the main model, and why in one asyncio.gather?
    scratchpad, last N turns, connectors, running agents, screen
  • L2 How do LLM tokens reach TTS before the reply text is finished?
    asyncio.Queue of reply deltas feeding Cartesia WebSocket TTS
  • L2 The model outputs structured JSON. How did you stream fields out of half-finished JSON?
    incremental extractor, 30-char tail for split markers, decodes escapes
  • L2 Each audio chunk carries the exact words in it. Why?
    captions sync; seal turn to words actually heard after interrupt
  • L2 Deepgram Flux vs Nova-3: why two profiles at first, and why one later?
    active end-of-turn vs passive diarization; one socket avoids reconnect on toggle
  • L2 Deepgram closes idle sockets. How did you keep transcription alive through long silences?
    8 s KeepAlive, in-place reconnect, drop chunks not session
  • L2 How do you avoid losing the last words when a session stops or switches mode?
    CloseStream, bounded 2–3 s drain before cancel
  • L2 Noise, coughs, doors and AiRA's own voice: how does Omni avoid treating them as a user turn?
    speech counts only when transcript has words; device echo cancellation
  • L3 What is the backpressure story when TTS is slower than the LLM, or the phone's network is slow?
  • L3 Why not WebRTC? What would you gain on mobile networks?
  • L3 What did you build vs teammates in the voice path?
    mine: Omni files, STT path, token→TTS queue; teammates: Cartesia adapters, FFmpeg

Follow-up chain

  • L2 What is the "voice slot" and what bug did it fix?
    Redis-locked owner so two overlapping turns never speak together
  • L2 Async tools: a tool takes 40 s. What does the user hear and how does the result come back?
    turn seals early; result returns on same call id as system turn
  • L3 Omni later moved from Sonnet to an OpenAI model. What changed in the voice path when the provider changed?

1.6 Barge-in, the latency budget, and the voice numbers on your resume

Learn: bullets.md § aira-client items 1–2 + § aira-api_s7 · DHANESH_AIRA_CONTRIBUTIONS.md aira-client features 7 and 19 · Pipecat "Interruptions" (docs.pipecat.ai) · AIE ch9 "TTFT/TPOT" (pdf p436–439)

  • L1 What is barge-in?
  • L1 What is time-to-first-audio and why does it matter more than total latency in voice?
  • L2 Your resume says "detects the user talking over it within about 200 ms". How did you measure 200 ms?
    two consecutive ~100 ms chunks above −45 dBFS; detection, not end to end
  • L2 Walk me through barge-in step by step: what is detected where, and what gets cancelled in what order?
  • L2 Why did barge-in first fire only after the final transcript, and what was wrong with that?
    player already torn down; backend kept synthesizing unheard audio
  • L2 Why does stop_voice cancel the TTS receiver before closing the audio window?
    already-synthesized audio must never play after interrupt
  • L2 Full duplex on iOS: how does the mic avoid hearing AiRA's own voice?
    .voiceChat session mode, VoiceProcessingIO echo cancellation
  • L2 What happens to the half-spoken answer after an interruption?
    held/parked, carried into next turn as "never heard" with reason
  • L2 Give me a latency budget for one voice turn: STT final, gate, retrieval, first token, first audio.
  • L2 How did you instrument speech latency?
    STT connect/first transcript, TTS first audio; p50–p99 dashboard per provider
  • L2 "Replaced 3 voice pipelines and 17,000 lines." Which three, and what was duplicated across them?
    live mode, chat, onboarding + websocket v1; ~17.8k lines deleted
  • L3 What are your actual p50 and p95 time-to-first-audio numbers? If you don't know them, why not?
  • L3 Energy threshold barge-in fires on a slammed door. How do you trade false barge-ins vs missed ones?
  • L3 "Crowd mode": several people talking. Why withhold barge-in then?
    others' speech would constantly cut AiRA; screen wait flags still released
  • L3 Deleting 17k lines of teammates' pipelines: how did you get buy-in and make sure nothing broke?

Follow-up chain

  • L2 The 200 ms is detection. What is the time from user speech to AiRA's audio actually stopping on the phone?
  • L2 Is the cancel sent on the wire at speech onset or after the transcript now?
    onset; client sends cancel if reply is playing, then clears queue
  • L3 How would you prove the barge-in number to me with data, not reasoning?

1.7 Scaling WebSockets, cross-worker coordination and crash safety

Learn: bullets.md § aira-api_s6 ("cross-worker features reliable") + § aira-api_s7 (write-ahead turn log) · nginx.org/en/docs/http/websocket.html · DDIA ch8 "Process Pauses" + ch9 "Linearizability" · redis.io/docs/latest/develop/interact/pubsub/

  • L1 Why are WebSocket connections hard to load-balance compared with HTTP requests?
  • L1 What is a sticky session? Did you need one?
  • L2 The stream for a turn may run on a different worker than the one holding the socket. How does output reach the phone?
    publish on Redis notify channel; socket owner forwards
  • L2 How does "stop generating" reach the right worker?
    Redis broadcast; every worker adds key to in-memory set; checked per event
  • L2 Why check an in-memory set on every token instead of asking Redis?
    no Redis round trip per token
  • L2 A late cancel arrives after the turn finished. How do you stop it killing the next answer?
    stale markers cleared when a new turn starts
  • L2 Your pub/sub subscriber used to die forever on one error. What did you change?
    reconnect loop, backoff 1 s→30 s, keepalive, no read timeout
  • L2 Messages in one session must never interleave. How did you guarantee order?
    per-session Redis lock; later messages buffered, merged, re-queued
  • L2 What is the Redis turn buffer and why use get-and-delete to drain it?
    atomic claim so two workers never process same utterances
  • L2 What is the Omni turn write-ahead log? What is in it and when is it deleted?
    Redis log of opener, responses, tool results; deleted when Mongo row seals
  • L2 The server restarts mid-turn. What does the user see, and what does recover() do at boot?
  • L2 WebSocket close code 1006 kept paging Slack. What did you do and why was it safe?
  • L3 You deploy a new version. What happens to 500 open voice sessions? How would you drain them?
  • L3 How many concurrent WebSockets can one FastAPI worker hold? What limits it first?
  • L3 Design this for 100k concurrent voice users. Where does per-connection state live?
    gateway tier for sockets; stateless turn workers; Redis Cluster sharding by user

Follow-up chain

  • L2 A Redis lock holder crashes. How long until the session is usable again?
    TTL on lock (e.g. 600 s); discuss shorter lease + renewal
  • L3 Redis lock with TTL is not safe under GC pauses or clock jumps. Does that matter here? What are fencing tokens?
  • L3 Two workers both believe they hold the session lock. What is the worst outcome in your system?

1.8 Long-term memory: the design (knowledge graph plus vectors)

Learn: bullets.md § aira-api_s1 · DHANESH_AIRA_CONTRIBUTIONS.md s1 features 5, 8–10 · AIE ch6 "Memory" (pdf p324–329) · AIE ch6 "Retrieval Optimization" (pdf p291–297) · DDIA ch2 "Graph-like Data Models" (pdf p70–84)

  • L1 Short-term vs mid-term vs long-term memory in AiRA: what is each and where is it stored?
    Redis working memory; MTM clusters in Qdrant; LTM facts, groups, AiRA Notes
  • L1 Why not just put the whole conversation history into the prompt?
  • L1 Why a graph plus vectors instead of vectors alone?
  • L2 What is a node and what is an edge in your Memgraph graph? Where do edge weights come from?
    topic nodes; LLM-scored relevance_score on edges from fixed vocabulary
  • L2 Explain the weighted traversal: why multiply edge scores along a path?
    product drops long chains of weak links below threshold
  • L2 Why must the traversal never walk through the user's own node?
    user hub links to everything; walking it returns whole graph
  • L2 How did you bound graph queries?
    depth shrinks 6→3 as seeds grow; max 200 nodes
  • L2 Walk me through the read path for a question like "what did I plan for Goa?"
    embed → similar topics → intent LLM picks topics → traversal + scoped note search
  • L2 What is the query-intent step and what does its one LLM call return?
    topics, rewritten statement, web-search flag, progress message
  • L2 Why embed an LLM-rewritten statement instead of the raw user message?
    pronouns resolved from recent turns; cleaner search
  • L2 Memory payloads are encrypted in Qdrant. How does retrieval stay fast?
    concurrent decrypt into deep copies across six collections
  • L2 Why did the team move from six memory collections to "topic-only" memory at the end of August 2025?
  • L3 Graph traversal vs vector search: give a real question where the graph found something the vector search missed.
  • L3 What is MIND (Memory via Intent-driven Narrowing & Dense Retrieval) and what were its four retrieval stages?
    soft-tag search → LLM rewrite + seed topics → bounded expansion → dense notes
  • L3 What exactly did you build in memory vs Ananda and Sumit?
    mine: schemas, traversals, indexes, batch writes, keep-alive, storage_v2; theirs: skeletons, storage LLM calls

Follow-up chain

  • L2 Memgraph is in-memory. What happens to memory on a Memgraph restart?
  • L2 How did you make the Memgraph connection self-heal?
    verify before use, recreate driver on ServiceUnavailable, 60 s keep-alive ping
  • L3 In October 2025 the chat stopped using graph traversal for scratchpads. Why roll back your own design?

1.9 Memory lifecycle: writes, consolidation, contradictions, deletion — and LongMemEval

Learn: bullets.md § aira-api_s5 item 6 (COSMOS) + § aira-api-bg · DHANESH_AIRA_CONTRIBUTIONS.md s5 feature 18 · LongMemEval paper (Wu et al., 2024, arXiv) · AIE ch4 "Design Your Evaluation Pipeline" (pdf p224–232)

  • L1 What is LongMemEval and what does it test?
    long-term chat memory: extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal, knowledge updates, abstention
  • L1 When are memories written: during the turn or after? Why?
  • L2 Your resume says "over 95% on LongMemEval". Is that your result or the team's, and which variant?
    95.2% LongMemEval-S, MIND paper, four co-authors; team result
  • L2 What was your part in the LongMemEval run?
    memory engine pieces; timestamp parsing for eval harness; say exactly
  • L2 "Under 3 s" — 3 s for what exactly, measured where, at which percentile?
    team figure; no measurement in code; be honest
  • L2 How did you make one conversation turn cost a fixed number of DB calls?
    one prefetch scroll; one Qdrant batch upsert each; Cypher UNWIND nodes/edges
  • L2 What does the COSMOS "flush" do?
    quiet MTM clusters → LLM distils atomic facts and note ops → LTM
  • L2 How are contradictions resolved?
    top-3 LTM facts above cosine 0.88, cheap "supersedes?" LLM call, delete superseded
  • L2 What is time-decay re-ranking and why are strong matches exempt?
    score × exp(−0.0006·age_hours), overfetch 3×; ≥0.90 keeps old exact memories
  • L2 What are AiRA Notes and why store them as ordered blocks?
    append/replace touch blocks, not whole note
  • L2 What did the aira-api-bg consolidation service do every 12 hours?
    scan Qdrant, HDBSCAN cluster, LLM merge, re-embed, write back
  • L2 A user says "delete everything you know about me". What exactly gets deleted, and from which stores?
  • L2 "I moved from Bangalore to Pune." Walk me through how the old fact is replaced.
  • L3 How do you stop memory from growing until it fills the context window?
  • L3 How would you evaluate memory quality yourself, without LongMemEval?
  • L3 A secret-seeded permutation and sign-flip of stored vectors keeps cosine unchanged. What does it protect, and what doesn't it?
    raw embeddings unreadable without seed; similarity leakage remains
  • L3 What exactly did you build in COSMOS vs teammates?
    mine: flush to LTM, contradictions, groups, notes, decay, browse API; Ananda: MTM store

Follow-up chain

  • L2 A flush writes facts, then crashes before deleting the cluster. What happens on the next run?
  • L2 Greetings and "thanks" skip retrieval and memory writes. Who decides — the LLM or code?
    code rule: no statement and no entities; later skip_retrieval flag
  • L3 The LLM extracts a wrong fact about the user. How would the user ever find and fix it?

1.10 Gmail and Calendar agents, and the onboarding job that reads 1,000 emails

Learn: bullets.md § aira-api_s2 item 6, § aira-api_s3, § aira-api_s4 · developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/web-server · developers.google.com/gmail/api/guides/batch · developers.google.com/gmail/api/reference/quota · developers.google.com/gmail/api/guides/push

  • L1 Access token vs refresh token: what is each and how long does each live?
  • L1 What is an OAuth scope? Which scopes did AiRA ask for?
    narrowed to gmail.modify, calendar.events, drive.file
  • L2 Walk me through connecting Gmail: consent URL, callback, token storage, first scrape.
  • L2 How does refresh-on-401 work and why a decorator?
    catch 401, decrypt refresh token, refresh, re-encrypt, retry once
  • L2 Google returns no refresh token on later sign-ins. What broke and how did you fix it?
    keep stored refresh token; prompt=consent on connector URLs
  • L2 What is incremental authorization and how did your per-scope token store work?
    tokeninfo for granted scopes; encrypted user_scopes row per scope
  • L2 What is the Gmail Batch API and why build the multipart request by hand?
    up to 100 GETs per multipart/mixed request; regex-parse response
  • L2 Walk me through the onboarding job: list, batch fetch, clean, summarize, combine.
    stream ids, batch API, strip HTML/headers, parallel map, LLM reduce
  • L2 Why map-reduce instead of one big LLM call over 1,000 emails?
  • L2 Why did batch size change 100 → 20 → 30 → 25? What were you trading?
    rate limits/quota vs LLM context per batch
  • L2 How does Gmail push work end to end?
    users.watch → Pub/Sub → webhook → history since id → summarize
  • L2 The OAuth state once carried the user id directly. What is wrong with that and what replaced it?
    not anti-CSRF; HMAC-signed state with uid field
  • L3 What Gmail quotas did you hit or design for? What happens to the onboarding job at 10k users signing up in one day?
  • L3 Scheduled jobs run with no user present. How do they get a valid token?
    load and decrypt stored token from Mongo; refresh on 401
  • L3 What exactly did you build vs teammates in the Google connector code?
    mine: Gmail/Calendar/Sheets agents, scope store, refresh decorators; later connector core Ananda's

Follow-up chain

  • L2 A user revokes access in their Google account. What does AiRA notice and when?
  • L2 "Email Rahul" — how does AiRA find the right Rahul?
    Metaphone codes of sender names embedded in Qdrant, threshold 0.75
  • L3 Delete email is permanent. How did you stop the agent deleting the wrong one?
    tool description forces search + confirm; later ask-tier approval

1.11 Tools and agent loops: typed tools → registry → APEX → one flattened loop

Learn: bullets.md § aira-api_s2 item 7, § aira-api_s3, § aira-api_s5 item 5, § aira-api_s7 item 2 · anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents · AIE ch6 "Tools" + "Planning" (pdf p302–322)

  • L1 What is tool calling / function calling? How does the model "call" a function?
  • L1 What is an agent loop? When does it stop?
  • L2 How did your typed tool framework turn a Pydantic model into a schema the LLM sees?
    model_json_schema, cycle-safe $ref inlining, descriptions on every arg
  • L2 How do access tokens and user ids reach a tool without the model ever seeing them?
    Field(exclude=True); injected just before execution
  • L2 What is progressive tool disclosure and what problem did it solve?
    agent summaries first; full schemas only for chosen agent
  • L2 What was APEX and why did you build it as a separate agent?
    Claude loop, parallel tools, 3 meta-tools, 180 s tool timeout
  • L2 What is the circuit breaker in APEX?
    stop after 5 consecutive turns where every tool failed
  • L2 Why did you flatten APEX into the main chat loop?
    one model, fewer hand-offs, simpler state, user sees steps live
  • L2 What is the unified tool registry and what gates run on every dispatch?
    resolve, agent, surface, connector linked, schema, then handler
  • L2 How does tool_search find a deferred tool?
    lexical match plus cosine over embeddings precomputed at startup
  • L2 Bad tool arguments from the model: crash, retry, or tell the model?
    return a tool error the model can fix
  • L3 Why must tool arrays be byte-identical across sessions?
    keeps provider prompt-cache prefix stable
  • L3 How do you stop an agent loop from running forever or burning money?
    iteration caps (25→5, later 20), timeouts, stuck detection, token budgets
  • L3 8 agents, ~100 tools. How do you know the model picks the right tool? Did you measure it?
  • L3 What exactly did you build vs Shashwat in the 2025 orchestrator?
    his orchestrator loop; my typed framework, credential injection, registry wiring

1.12 The durable background agent runtime (3 tasks per user)

Learn: bullets.md § aira-api_s7 ("durable background-agent runtime") + § local-uncommitted-and-unpushed · DURABLE_WORKERS_IMPLEMENTED.md · AIRA_DURABLE_WORKERS_PLAN.md · DDIA ch11 "Messaging systems" (pdf p449–454) · temporal.io/how-it-works

  • L1 What is a durable agent and why can't a long task just be an asyncio task?
  • L1 What kinds of background tasks exist?
    research, canvas_doc, connector, browser
  • L2 Walk me through start_task: what is checked before a row is queued?
    browsing enabled, skill exists, services connected, valid parent run
  • L2 How does the "up to 3 tasks in parallel per user" gate work?
    Redis INCR slots:{user}; over 3 → DECR, stay queued
  • L2 The Mongo claim fails after the counter was incremented. How do you stop the counter drifting?
    decrement on failed claim; minute sweep repairs drift
  • L2 Why the braces in slots:{user_id}?
    Redis Cluster hash tag; one user's keys on one shard
  • L2 Draw the state machine of a run row.
    queued → running → sleeping/paused → ready/failed/stopped
  • L2 What is a wait and what is the inbox?
    why it sleeps with deadline; steer/answer/approval messages to wake it
  • L2 How do you make sure a late writer can never reopen a finished run?
    guarded transition only from expected status via find_one_and_update
  • L2 What happens at boot to runs that were mid-flight?
    reset counters; resume rows with checkpoint; fail rows without
  • L2 What does the minute sweep do?
    due wakes, deadline expiry, counter drift, lost "done" turns, checkpoint retention
  • L2 How does a task report back into the conversation?
    [AGENT_PROGRESS], [AGENT_NOTE], [AGENT_DONE] system turns, push notification
  • L3 How does the agent loop detect it is stuck?
    same tool + args 3×, or 5 steps of already-seen results
  • L3 Why build this on Mongo + Redis instead of Temporal, Celery or a cloud workflow service?
  • L3 This is ~21k lines committed in two days in October 2026. How much was AI-assisted, and how did you review it?
  • L3 What exactly is yours here vs teammates' code underneath?
    runtime and integrations mine; Google OAuth, token encryption, IRIS base mostly teammates'

Follow-up chain

  • L2 The 4th task arrives while 3 run. What does the user see, and who admits it later?
    queued with position; done-callback frees slot, admits oldest
  • L3 A process restart caught an ask_main mid-settlement. How did you avoid running it twice?
    scan checkpoint for unsettled ask; sleep on it again

1.15 The credential vault: AES-256-GCM, envelope encryption, Azure Key Vault

Learn: bullets.md § aira-api_s7 ("per-user credential vault") + § aira-api-bg item 6 · KEY_VAULT_KEYS_DEEP_DIVE.md · learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/keys/about-keys · cloud.google.com/kms/docs/envelope-encryption

  • L1 What is envelope encryption? Data key vs key-encryption key.
  • L1 What does GCM give you that CBC does not?
    authenticated encryption; tag detects tampering
  • L2 What is the nonce in AES-GCM, how big is yours, and what happens if you reuse one?
    12 random bytes; reuse leaks plaintext XOR and forgery
  • L2 What is associated data and what did you bind into it?
    user_id:handle:field; ciphertext moved elsewhere won't open
  • L2 Where does the data key live, and in what form?
    only wrapped by Key Vault RSA-OAEP-256 KEK, with version
  • L2 Why RSA-OAEP-256 wrapping in Key Vault instead of encrypting every value in Key Vault directly?
    latency, cost, rate limits; one unwrap per user key
  • L2 How does key rotation work?
    at boot, re-wrap stale keys with current KEK version, 8 at a time
  • L2 What is crypto-shredding and how does "revoke all" use it?
    blank wrapped key; every old ciphertext becomes unreadable
  • L2 How are one-time codes handled?
    encrypted, Redis 5 minutes, get-and-delete; single use, only for waiting run
  • L2 The data key is cached in memory 15 minutes. Why, and what are the risks?
    avoid unwrap per call; epoch counter, forget_user after task
  • L2 Saving a password is only accepted for a run waiting on exactly that site. Why?
    no unsolicited secrets; password never passes through the model
  • L3 How do you make sure a password never shows up in logs, error messages or validation errors?
    sensitive routes strip input/ctx; fixed "act failed" messages
  • L3 Your process is compromised while running. What can the attacker read? What can't they?
  • L3 Why is a login typed only when the page's registrable domain matches the handle's host?
    stops phishing look-alike pages receiving credentials
  • L3 Explain why a 96-bit random nonce is fine for your volume but would worry you at billions of encryptions per key.

1.17 Reminders (IRIS), cron locks and bursty messages (TEMPEX)

Learn: bullets.md § aira-api_s3 (IRIS, TEMPEX v2) + § aira-api_s5 items 4, 10 + § aira-api_s7 last item · DDIA ch11 "Fault tolerance" (pdf p482–484) · redis.io/docs/latest/develop/use/patterns/distributed-locks/ · martin.kleppmann.com/2016/02/08/how-to-do-distributed-locking.html

  • L1 At-most-once vs at-least-once vs exactly-once: define each with a reminder example.
  • L1 What is a distributed lock? How do you take and release one in Redis?
    SET key token NX PX ttl; Lua compare-and-delete release
  • L2 Walk me through IRIS: how does "remind me every Monday at 9" become a fired reminder?
  • L2 Why two tables (UserTask hourly planning, GlobalTask run-now queue) in the first design?
    every-minute cron scans only the small run-now table
  • L2 Why move recurring tasks forward from the previous trigger time, not from now?
    stops schedule drift
  • L2 With three API instances, every cron fired three times. How did you fix it?
    Redis lock per job per tick (~50–55 s TTL)
  • L2 Your resume says "fires at most once, even after a crash". Exactly how?
    settle due rows in one bulk_write before executing; crash loses, never repeats
  • L2 Why choose at-most-once for reminders instead of at-least-once? What does the user see on a crash?
  • L2 The LLM writes "notify" or "ping" instead of remind. How did you handle it?
    Pydantic before-validator maps synonyms to the one valid name
  • L2 What problem does TEMPEX solve?
    users send 3 short messages; merge into one reply, cancel stale runs
  • L2 TEMPEX v2 used Lua scripts and an ordered stream queue; the redesign used two fields. Why simplify?
    pending_query + pending_trace_id, ownership checkpoints; fewer races, no polling
  • L2 A user says "actually make it 6pm" while a task is running. How did that reach the running task?
    appended to task execution logs; orchestrator re-reads each iteration
  • L3 Is "at most once" really guaranteed if the Mongo write succeeds but the process dies before the reminder is sent?
  • L3 A Redis lock TTL of 55 s and a job that takes 70 s. What happens? How would you fix it properly?
  • L3 Design reminders for 10M users with per-second precision. Would you keep the minute sweep?
    time-bucketed sorted sets or delay queue; partition by time
  • L3 What exactly did you build in IRIS and TEMPEX vs teammates?
    IRIS design, April port, TEMPEX mine; later iris_ent mostly Shashwat's

Follow-up chain

  • L3 The global cron deletes due tasks before running them. What did that fix and what did it give up?
    no retry storms every minute; a failed task is lost

2.21 Trading backtests and the TradingView MCP server

Learn: ../../trading/trading_equations.md · Advances in Financial Machine Learning ch.11 "The Dangers of Backtesting" · Art and Science of Trading ch.15 "Opening range" (pdf p533) · modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/learn/architecture · chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/

  • L1 What question were the backtests trying to answer?
    do retail strategies make money on NSE after real costs?
  • L1 What is lookahead bias?
  • L1 What is survivorship bias?
  • L1 What is overfitting in a backtest, and what is walk-forward / out-of-sample testing?
  • L1 What is MCP (Model Context Protocol)? What are tools, resources and transports?
  • L2 How did your simulator avoid lookahead?
    next-open fills; higher-timeframe filters use only closed bars; tests
  • L2 The universe was today's Nifty 200. How much did that inflate results?
    momentum 35%/yr vs the real index 14.6%/yr
  • L2 How did you model costs, and why did they decide the short timeframes?
    FYERS charges + slippage; ~₹400 intraday vs ~₹2,287 delivery round trip
  • L2 The "best" settings died at 0.02–0.03% slippage. What does that tell you?
  • L2 What is a random-entry placebo, and why compare against it?
    same exits, random entries; strategy must beat luck
  • L2 How did you check the simulator itself was right?
    hand-computed indicators in tests; trades re-checked against raw candles
  • L2 How did you split in-sample and out-of-sample, and what was the pass rule?
  • L2 Which filters held up out of sample?
    walk-forward 200-day market filter helped; vol targeting, GARCH, HMM didn't
  • L2 How does the TradingView MCP server control the app?
    Chrome DevTools Protocol on a debug port; 84 tools
  • L2 You didn't write the MCP server. What did you build around it?
    registration, port fix, data exporter, Pine strategies, re-costing scripts
  • L3 You tested hundreds of variants. How do you avoid fooling yourself?
    out-of-sample, placebo, few parameters, deflated Sharpe
  • L3 You had only 3.5 months of 5-minute bars. How much can you trust an intraday result?
  • L3 The MCP relies on undocumented TradingView internals. What are the risks for an agent built on it?
    breaks on update; pin version; health checks
  • L3 An LLM agent drives charts and writes Pine Script. How do you guarantee it never places a real trade?
    no order tools exposed; separate broker keys; confirmations
  • L3 Give your verdict on retail indicator strategies in 30 seconds.
    most lose after costs; momentum rotation and weekly pullback survived

4. DSA — data structures, algorithms and the systems they power

open this topic alone → · 718 questions

4.1 Complexity analysis, recursion and the call stack

Learn: bigocheatsheet.com · neetcode.io/courses · wiki.python.org/moin/TimeComplexity · usaco.guide/bronze/time-comp · Introduction to Algorithms (CLRS) ch3–4

  • L1 What do Big-O, Big-Θ and Big-Ω describe?
    upper, tight and lower bounds on growth
  • L1 Best, average and worst case — is that the same thing as O, Θ and Ω?
    no: cases pick inputs; O/Θ/Ω bound functions
  • L1 Rank these: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²), O(2ⁿ), O(n!).
  • L1 What is space complexity? Does the input itself count?
    auxiliary vs total space; say which you mean
  • L1 Why do we drop constants and lower-order terms? When do constants matter in practice?
  • L1 What is the complexity of a loop that halves n each step? Of a nested loop where the inner one runs i times?
  • L2 Why is appending to a dynamic array (Python list, JS array) O(1) amortised?
    geometric growth; total copying ≤ 2n
  • L2 What is amortised analysis? Aggregate vs accounting vs potential method, one line each.
  • L2 Amortised vs average case: what is the difference?
    amortised is a guarantee over any sequence; average assumes a distribution
  • L2 If a dynamic array grew by +10 slots instead of doubling, what would append cost?
    O(n) amortised: arithmetic series of copies
  • L2 Why is hash map lookup "O(1)", and when is it O(n)?
    average with good hash and bounded load; collisions, adversarial keys
  • L2 Given n ≤ 10⁵, which complexities fit a 1-second limit? n ≤ 20? n ≤ 10⁹?
    ~10⁸ simple ops/s: n log n; 2ⁿ; log n
  • L2 Cost of x in list vs x in set in Python? Of arr.includes(x) vs set.has(x) in JS?
  • L2 What does building a string with += in a loop cost in Python and JS, and what do you do instead?
    immutable strings → O(n²) worst; join / array push
  • L2 Why can't a comparison sort beat O(n log n)?
    decision tree with n! leaves; log(n!) = Θ(n log n)
  • L2 How do you state complexity with two inputs (graph V and E, two strings m and n)?
  • L3 Why is building a heap bottom-up O(n), not O(n log n)?
    most nodes sit near leaves; sum of heights is O(n)
  • L3 What is pseudo-polynomial time? Why is the 0/1 knapsack DP not "polynomial"?
    polynomial in value W, exponential in its bit length
  • L3 What does Big-O hide that bites you in production?
    constants, cache misses, allocation, GC, I/O dominating CPU
  • L3 P, NP, NP-complete in one sentence each — and an NP-hard problem you would meet at work.
    scheduling, bin packing → heuristics, approximation

Recursion and the call stack

  • L1 What happens on the call stack when a function calls itself? What is in a stack frame?
  • L1 What two parts does every recursive function need? What is Python's default recursion limit?
    base case + progress; ~1000, RecursionError
  • L2 What is the space complexity of recursive DFS on a balanced tree? On a skewed tree?
    O(h): O(log n) vs O(n)
  • L2 Draw the recursion tree for naive Fibonacci. What is its complexity, and what does memoisation change?
  • L2 State the Master theorem idea and solve T(n)=2T(n/2)+n, T(n)=T(n/2)+1, T(n)=2T(n/2)+1.
    n log n; log n; n
  • L2 What is tail recursion? Do CPython or V8 optimise it?
    no tail-call optimisation in either
  • L2 What does slicing arr[1:] cost inside a recursive function, and what do you pass instead?
    O(k) copy per call; pass indices
  • L2 How does functools.lru_cache / @cache turn exponential recursion into polynomial? What are its pitfalls?
    hashable args, unbounded memory, depth unchanged
  • L3 Your recursive solution crashes in Python at n = 10⁵. What are your options?
    explicit stack, bottom-up, raise limit + bigger thread stack
  • L3 Convert a recursive DFS to an iterative one with an explicit stack. Where do pre- and post-order work go?

4.2 How to approach a coding round

Learn: techinterviewhandbook.org/coding-interview-techniques/ · techinterviewhandbook.org/algorithms/study-cheatsheet/ · interviewing.io · docs.python.org/3/library/collections.html · docs.python.org/3/library/bisect.html

  • L1 What do you do in the first three minutes after hearing a problem?
    restate, clarify, small example, edge cases, constraints
  • L1 Which clarifying questions do you always ask?
    size, value ranges, negatives, duplicates, sorted, empty, in-place, output format
  • L1 Why say the brute force and its complexity out loud before optimising?
  • L1 Which edge cases do you test before saying "done"?
    empty, one element, duplicates, negatives, all equal, overflow, max size
  • L2 How do you go from brute force to optimal? Name the usual moves.
    hash/prefix precompute, sort, two pointers, heap, binary search, DP
  • L2 How do constraints hint at the intended complexity?
    n≤20 → 2ⁿ; 10³ → n²; 10⁵ → n log n
  • L2 You are stuck 15 minutes in. What do you say and do?
  • L2 How do you dry-run code on an example without running it, and what do you track?
  • L2 The interviewer asks "can you do better?" How do you decide if better is possible?
    lower bounds: must read input; sorting bound
  • L2 Python: which built-ins must you know cold?
    deque, Counter, defaultdict, heapq, bisect, itertools, functools.cache, sort keys
  • L2 TypeScript/JS: which built-ins do you rely on, and what is missing?
    Map, Set, array methods; no heap, deque, sorted map
  • L2 array.shift() in JS is O(n). How do you write a fast queue for BFS?
    head index pointer, or ring buffer
  • L2 How do you explain complexity at the end — what exactly do you say?
  • L3 Machine coding round (90 min: parking lot, Splitwise, snake game): how is it scored differently from DSA?
    runnable code, extensibility, clean classes, separation, tests
  • L3 You spot a bug after the interviewer has moved on. Do you raise it? How?
  • L3 How do you practise so NeetCode 150 patterns stick?
    timed 25 min, redo failures after 3 days, explain aloud

10.1 Why Redis is fast — the threading model

  • L1 Why is Redis so fast?
    in memory, single-threaded execution, I/O multiplexing, compact data structures, simple protocol
  • L1 Is Redis single-threaded? Be precise.
    commands run on one thread; helper threads for I/O, freeing memory, fsync
  • L1 Rough latency and throughput of one Redis instance?
    sub-millisecond; around 100k+ simple ops/s per instance
  • L1 What is RESP?
    the Redis wire protocol; RESP3 arrived in Redis 6
  • L2 What is I/O multiplexing (epoll / kqueue), and how does the Redis event loop use it?
  • L2 Why did Redis choose one thread for commands? What does that buy you?
    no locks, every command atomic, simple; CPU rarely the bottleneck
  • L2 What do io-threads in Redis 6+ do, and what do they not do?
    socket reads/writes and parsing; commands still run on one thread
  • L2 One command takes 2 seconds. What happens to every other client?
  • L2 Name commands that can block the event loop.
    KEYS, sync FLUSHALL, DEL of huge keys, HGETALL/SMEMBERS on huge keys, long Lua
  • L2 UNLINK vs DEL. What is lazy freeing?

  • L2 The fragmentation ratio is below 1. What does that mean?
    memory is being swapped to disk: bad
  • L2 How do you cut memory for 100M tiny keys?
    bucket into small hashes (listpack), shorter key names, TTLs
  • L2 Latency spikes every few minutes. List the suspects.

    blocks and builds a huge reply; use HSCAN

    per-client buffers, maxclients, missing pooling

11.1 The interview framework

Learn: hellointerview.com/learn/system-design/in-a-hurry/delivery · System Design Interview (Xu) vol1 ch3 · github.com/donnemartin/system-design-primer · DDIA ch1 (pdf p23–42)

  • L1 Walk me through the steps you follow in a system design interview.
    requirements, estimates, API, data model, high-level, deep dives, trade-offs
  • L1 What is the difference between functional and non-functional requirements? Give two of each for a chat app.
  • L1 Which non-functional requirements do you always ask about?
    scale, latency, availability vs consistency, durability, cost, security
  • L1 Why should you say what is out of scope early?
  • L2 How many core features do you pick for a 45-minute round, and how do you choose them?
  • L2 How much time do you spend on each phase of a 45-minute design?
  • L2 What makes a good API definition in a design round? What do you leave out?
  • L2 How do you go from the API to the data model? What do you decide about each entity?
  • L2 What should the first high-level diagram contain, and what should it not contain yet?
  • L2 How do you choose which part to deep-dive into if the interviewer does not pick?
  • L2 The interviewer says "assume infinite scale". How do you respond?
  • L2 How do you state a trade-off so that it sounds like engineering and not guessing?
    option A vs B, what each costs, which requirement decides
  • L2 When do you do estimation, and when do you skip it?
  • L2 What are the most common mistakes candidates make in design rounds?
    jumping to tech, no numbers, no trade-offs, overbuilding, silence
  • L2 How do you handle a requirement you have never built before mid-interview?
  • L3 The interviewer keeps pushing "what if 10× more traffic?". How do you find the next bottleneck each time?
  • L3 How do you wrap up: bottlenecks, failure modes, monitoring, what you'd do next — what goes in each?
  • L3 How do you design for a 5-person startup differently from a design for Google scale? Give a concrete example.
  • L3 Tell me about a real system you designed at AiRA end to end, using this framework.
  • L3 What would you do differently in that AiRA design today?

11.2 Back-of-envelope estimation and numbers to know

Learn: System Design Interview (Xu) vol1 ch2 · gist.github.com/jboner/2841832 (latency numbers) · github.com/donnemartin/system-design-primer#powers-of-two-table · DDIA ch1 "Describing load" (pdf p31)

  • L1 How many seconds in a day, roughly? Why do people round it to 10⁵?
  • L1 1 million requests per day is about how many QPS?
    ~12 QPS
  • L1 What is the usual ratio of peak to average traffic?
    2–3×, more for spiky events
  • L1 Powers of two: what are 2¹⁰, 2²⁰, 2³⁰, 2⁴⁰ in KB/MB/GB/TB terms?
  • L1 Latency numbers: L1 cache, RAM, SSD read, same-datacenter round trip, disk seek, cross-continent round trip.
    0.5 ns, 100 ns, ~100 µs, 0.5 ms, 10 ms, 150 ms
  • L1 How much downtime per year does 99.9% allow? 99.99%? 99.999%?
    ~8.8 h, ~53 min, ~5 min
  • L1 Roughly how many simple QPS can one Postgres node serve? One Redis node? One app server?
    ~5–10k, ~100k ops/s, ~1–5k RPS
  • L2 100M DAU, each user does 10 reads and 1 write a day. What are read QPS, write QPS and peak QPS?
  • L2 10M new posts a day at 1 KB each plus 10% with a 500 KB image. What is storage per day and per 5 years?
  • L2 How do you estimate bandwidth (ingress and egress) from QPS and payload size?
  • L2 How do you estimate how many servers you need? What do you assume per server?
  • L2 How do you estimate cache memory for "the hottest 20% of a day's reads"?
  • L2 How do you compute availability of two services in series? In parallel?
    series multiply; parallel 1 − product of failure rates
  • L2 How many WebSocket connections can one server hold, and what limits it?
    memory per connection, file descriptors, CPU for heartbeats
  • L2 What does an 80/20 rule mean in cache sizing, and when is it wrong?
  • L2 Why does reading 1 MB sequentially from memory vs SSD vs network vs disk matter for design?
  • L3 Your estimate says 2 servers are enough. Why might you still run 6?
  • L3 How do you estimate LLM cost per month for 1M users sending 20 messages a day?
  • L3 Estimate the number of GPUs needed to serve 1,000 concurrent streaming LLM sessions. What numbers do you need?
  • L3 The interviewer says your numbers are off by 10×. Which parts of your design change and which don't?

11.6 Caching

Learn: github.com/donnemartin/system-design-primer#cache · redis.io/solutions/caching/ · en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cache_stampede · DBI ch5 "Cache Eviction / Page Replacement" (pdf p148–156) · DDIA ch3 "Aggregation: Data cubes and materialized views" (pdf p120)

  • L1 Why cache? What does a cache trade for speed?
  • L1 Name the cache layers from client to database.
    browser, CDN, gateway, app in-memory, distributed (Redis), DB buffer pool
  • L1 What is cache hit ratio? What is a good one?
  • L1 What is TTL?
  • L1 Name the eviction policies.
    LRU, LFU, FIFO, random, TTL-based; Redis allkeys-lru etc.
  • L2 Cache-aside vs read-through vs write-through vs write-behind vs write-around: explain each.
  • L2 Which caching pattern would you use for a user profile, a product catalogue, a leaderboard, a session?
  • L2 What do you cache and what do you never cache?
    hot, read-heavy, tolerant of staleness; never secrets or per-request auth decisions blindly
  • L2 What is cache invalidation, and why is it called one of the two hard problems?
  • L2 On update: delete the cache key or update it? Why do most people delete?
    avoids race writing stale value
  • L2 Update DB then delete cache: describe the race that still leaves stale data.
    slow reader repopulates old value after delete; use short TTL, delayed double delete
  • L2 What is a cache stampede (thundering herd)? Three ways to prevent it.
    request coalescing/locks, early probabilistic refresh, stale-while-revalidate
  • L2 What is cache penetration (requests for keys that don't exist)? Fix?
    cache negatives, bloom filter
  • L2 What is cache avalanche (many keys expire at once)? Fix?
    jittered TTLs, warmup, multi-level cache

23.2 Multi-provider routing and the provider abstraction

  • L1 What is model routing? What is provider routing?
  • L1 Name the providers and models you support.
  • L2 How do you normalise different provider APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Azure OpenAI) into one interface?
    adapter per provider: request mapping, streaming event mapping, error mapping
  • L2 How do you map tool calls / function calling across providers that format them differently?
  • L2 What routing strategies do you support?
    static by model, weighted, lowest latency, lowest cost, failover chain, by tenant tier
  • L2 How does latency-based routing know which provider is fastest right now?
    rolling TTFT/latency windows per provider in memory or Redis
  • L2 How do you route between a cheap model and a strong model based on the request?
  • L2 How do you normalise error codes across providers so retries and breakers work consistently?
  • L2 How do you count tokens before sending, when each provider tokenises differently?
  • L2 How do you add a new provider without touching the core? What is the extension point?
  • L2 Model aliases (fast, smart) vs exact model names: why expose aliases?
  • L3 Fallback to a different model changes answer quality and format. When is fallback acceptable, and who decides?
  • L3 How do you handle provider-specific features (prompt caching, JSON mode, vision) that others lack?
  • L3 How do you A/B test a new model through the gateway?
  • L3 Learned routing (a classifier picks the model): how would you train and evaluate it?
  • L3 A provider silently changes model behaviour. How would the gateway detect it?

23.3 Streaming — SSE proxying

Learn: developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Server-sent_events/Using_server-sent_events · nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_proxy_module.html (proxy_buffering) · nodejs.org/en/learn/modules/backpressuring-in-streams · AIE ch9 "Inference Performance Metrics" (pdf p436–439; TTFT/TPOT)

  • L1 What is SSE? Why do LLM APIs stream with SSE rather than WebSockets?
  • L1 What does an SSE event look like on the wire?
    data: lines, blank line terminator, optional event:/id:
  • L2 How do you proxy a provider's stream to the client without buffering the whole response?
  • L2 How do you translate one provider's stream format into your common format on the fly?
  • L2 How do you count tokens and cost for a streamed response?
    final usage chunk (stream_options.include_usage) or count yourself
  • L2 What headers and proxy settings must be right for streaming to work through nginx / ingress / CDN?
  • L2 How do you handle backpressure when the client reads slower than the provider writes?
  • L2 Can you cache a streamed response? How?
    tee the stream; store on completion only; replay as a stream on hit
  • L2 What is TTFT through your gateway vs direct to the provider? Where is the extra time?
  • L2 How do you send heartbeats / keep-alive comments so idle proxies don't kill long streams?
  • L3 The provider fails after 200 tokens are already sent. Can you fall back to another provider mid-stream?
    usually no; send error event; client retries; or buffer-first mode
  • L3 How do you test streaming correctness and chunk boundaries (split UTF-8, split JSON)?
  • L3 Would you support WebSockets or the Realtime API (voice) in the gateway? What changes?

23.4 Semantic caching with Qdrant

Learn: AIE ch10 "Step 4. Reduce Latency with Caches" (pdf p484–487, exact + semantic caching) · qdrant.tech/documentation/ · github.com/zilliztech/GPTCache · AIE ch3 "Introduction to Embedding" (pdf p158–160, cosine similarity)

  • L1 Exact cache vs semantic cache: what is the difference?
  • L1 What is an embedding, and what is cosine similarity?
  • L2 Walk me through a semantic cache lookup step by step.
    normalise prompt → embed → ANN search in Qdrant → threshold → return
  • L2 What do you use as the cache key or embedding input: the last user message, the whole conversation, or a hash of the system prompt plus the message?
  • L2 How do you pick the similarity threshold? What happens if it's too low or too high?
  • L2 What is your hit rate, and how much latency and cost does a hit save?
  • L2 What does a semantic cache lookup cost on a miss, and when does it make things slower overall?
  • L2 Why check an exact-match Redis cache before the semantic cache?
  • L2 Which requests must never be cached?
    high temperature, tool calls, personal data, time-sensitive, cache: false
  • L2 How do you isolate the cache per tenant in Qdrant?
    payload filter on tenant_id with index, or collection per tenant
  • L2 How do you expire semantic cache entries? Does Qdrant have TTL?
  • L2 Why Qdrant and not Redis vector search, pgvector or Pinecone?
  • L2 Which embedding model did you use, and why that size?
  • L3 "What is the capital of France?" vs "What is not the capital of France?" — how does semantic caching get this wrong, and what is your guard?
  • L3 How do you evaluate that cached answers are still correct for the new question?
    offline labelled pairs, precision at threshold, sampled LLM-judge
  • L3 What is the HNSW index in Qdrant, and what do m and ef trade off?

23.5 Per-tenant rate limiting and quotas

Learn: stripe.com/blog/rate-limiters · redis.io/docs/latest/develop/interact/programmability/eval-intro/ · Redis in Action (Carlson) ch6–7 · AIE ch10 "Step 3. Add Model Router and Gateway" (pdf p482–484, gateway fallbacks and rate limits)

  • L1 What do you limit: requests per minute, tokens per minute, concurrent requests, or spend? Why each?
  • L1 Sliding window log vs sliding window counter vs token bucket: which did you choose?
  • L2 Show the Redis data structure and the Lua script for your sliding window.
    ZSET of timestamps or two fixed-window counters weighted
  • L2 Why a Lua script instead of separate Redis commands from Node?
  • L2 How do you rate limit by tokens when you don't know output tokens until the response ends?
    reserve estimate (max_tokens) up front, refund/adjust after
  • L2 How are limits configured per tenant and per API key, and how do changes take effect without a deploy?
  • L2 What headers do you return to clients?
    429, Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset
  • L2 How do you also respect the provider's own rate limits across all tenants?
    global per-provider budget, queue, spread across keys/deployments
  • L2 What does one rate-limit check cost in latency, and how many Redis round-trips?
  • L2 Hard limits vs soft limits vs monthly budgets: how do they differ in your design?
  • L3 Redis Cluster: how do you keep a tenant's keys on one slot?
    hash tags {tenant}
  • L3 Redis is down. Fail open or fail closed for rate limiting? What about for budgets?
    often open for RPM with local fallback limiter; closed for spend
  • L3 How do you stop one noisy tenant from hurting others even within their limits?
    fair queuing, concurrency caps, bulkheads per tier
  • L3 How accurate is your limiter under clock skew between pods?
  • L3 How did you test the limiter for correctness under concurrency?

23.6 Resilience — circuit breakers, retries, timeouts, fallback

Learn: martinfowler.com/bliki/CircuitBreaker.html · aws.amazon.com/builders-library/timeouts-retries-and-backoff-with-jitter/ · aws.amazon.com/builders-library/avoiding-fallback-in-distributed-systems/ · DBI ch8 "Cascading Failures" (pdf p292) · Release It! (Nygard)

  • L1 How does a circuit breaker work? Explain closed, open and half-open.
  • L1 Why exponential backoff, and why add jitter?
  • L2 What trips your breaker: error rate, consecutive failures, latency, or 429s? Over what window?
  • L2 Is the breaker per provider, per model, per region or per API key? Why that granularity?
  • L2 Is breaker state per pod or shared in Redis? Trade-offs.
    local is fast and simple; shared reacts consistently but adds dependency
  • L2 Which errors do you retry and which never?
    retry 429/5xx/timeouts; never 400/401/content-filter
  • L2 How do you honour a provider's Retry-After header?
  • L2 Full jitter vs equal jitter vs decorrelated jitter: which did you use?
  • L2 What timeouts did you set: connect, TTFT, idle-between-chunks, total? Why separate ones?
    TTFT timeout catches stuck providers before the long tail
  • L2 How does the fallback chain work, and how do you stop fallbacks from overloading the backup provider?
  • L2 What is a retry budget, and do you have one?
  • L2 Did you use a library (opossum, cockatiel, tenacity) or write it yourself? Why?
  • L3 Retries + fallback + client retries can multiply one request into nine calls. How do you prevent retry storms?
  • L3 Half-open sends a probe request. Do you use real user traffic or synthetic probes? Why?
  • L3 What is your graceful degradation when every provider is failing?
  • L3 How did you test the breaker and fallback?
    fault injection: mock provider returning 500/429/slow streams, chaos tests

    weighted fair queuing, aging, reserved capacity per lane

  • L3 How do priority queues work across 10 gateway pods? Local queues or shared?
  • L3 What is Little's law telling you about queue size at your target throughput and provider latency?

23.8 Usage tracking, cost per tenant, Kafka events

Learn: confluent.io/blog/exactly-once-semantics-are-possible-heres-how-apache-kafka-does-it/ · microservices.io/patterns/data/transactional-outbox.html · microservices.io/patterns/communication-style/idempotent-consumer.html · DDIA ch11 "Fault tolerance" (pdf p482–484)

  • L1 What do you record for each request for billing?
    tenant, key, model, provider, input/output/cached tokens, cost, latency, status, request id

    tenant id: per-tenant ordering and aggregation locality

    unique request id; insert ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING / dedupe table

  • L3 A client disconnects mid-stream. Do you bill the tokens generated so far? How do you know the count?

23.9 Security of the gateway

Learn: cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/REST_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html · zod.dev · helmetjs.github.io · learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/basic-concepts · genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/

  • L1 How do tenants authenticate to the gateway?
  • L1 Where do the provider API keys live?
    Key Vault / secrets manager; loaded via managed identity; never in env files or git

  • L2 How do you validate requests with Zod? What limits do you enforce?

  • L2 What does helmet add to a JSON API gateway, and what is irrelevant?
  • L2 How do you fetch provider keys from Key Vault without adding latency to every request?
    cache in memory with refresh; rotation picks up new version
  • L2 How do you rotate a provider key with zero downtime?
  • L2 How do you stop one tenant from reading another tenant's cache entries, logs or usage?
  • L2 Do you log prompts? How do you handle PII and data-retention requests?
  • L2 Bring-your-own-key (tenant supplies provider keys): how do you store them?
    envelope encryption per tenant, like the AiRA vault
  • L3 Should the gateway do prompt-injection or PII guardrails, or leave it to apps? Defend the boundary.

23.10 Postgres and Redis — data model, queries, migrations, locks

Learn: postgresql.org/docs/current/using-explain.html · postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-partitioning.html · pgbouncer.org/features.html · martin.kleppmann.com/2016/02/08/how-to-do-distributed-locking.html

  • L1 What lives in Postgres and what lives in Redis? Why?

23.15 Failure scenarios

Learn: sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/ · aws.amazon.com/builders-library/avoiding-fallback-in-distributed-systems/ · principlesofchaos.org

Scenarios

  • L2 OpenAI is down for 30 minutes. Walk me through what your gateway does, minute by minute.
  • L2 A provider returns 429s for everyone because you hit your org limit. What happens?
  • L2 Redis goes down. What still works: auth, rate limits, cache, breakers, locks?

    strict lookup timeout, skip cache, breaker on Qdrant
  • L2 Postgres is down. Can requests still be served?
  • L2 Kafka is down for an hour. Do you lose billing data?
  • L2 A client disconnects in the middle of a streamed response. What do you do with the provider stream, the tokens and the bill?
    abort upstream, record partial usage, no cache write
  • L2 The provider stream stalls for 60 seconds mid-response. What detects it and what does the client see?
  • L2 One tenant sends 50× their normal traffic. What protects everyone else?
  • L2 A tenant's key leaks and someone burns $5,000 in an hour. How would you have stopped it at $50?
  • L2 A deploy doubles p99 latency. How fast do you detect it and roll back?
  • L3 Cache poisoning: a wrong answer was cached and served 10,000 times. Detect, purge and prevent.
  • L3 Cost blowup: a client bug loops and calls the gateway in a tight retry loop. Where does it get stopped?
  • L3 A provider changes its streaming format without notice and your parser breaks. Blast radius and recovery?
  • L3 Fallback model returns a different JSON shape and breaks the client's parser. Whose bug is it?
  • L3 Retry storm: the primary recovers, but queued retries from every pod hit it at once. How do you prevent it?
  • L3 Clock skew breaks your sliding-window limiter on one pod. What symptoms would you see?
  • L3 A Kafka consumer rebalance replays an hour of usage events. Do tenants get double-billed?
  • L3 Key Vault is unreachable at startup. Do new pods start? Should they?
  • L3 A whole cloud region fails. What is your multi-region story, and is it worth it?

24. LLM fundamentals and AI engineering

open this topic alone → · 417 questions

24.1 Tokens and tokenization

Learn: HOL ch2 "LLM Tokenization" (pdf p60–78; BPE/WordPiece p65–73) · AIE ch2 "Multilingual Models" (pdf p75–79) · Karpathy "Let's build the GPT Tokenizer" (YouTube) · platform.openai.com/tokenizer

  • L1 What is a token?
  • L1 Why do LLMs work on tokens instead of characters or whole words?
  • L1 Roughly how many tokens is one English word? How many characters per token?
    ~1.3 tokens per word; ~4 characters per token
  • L1 What is a tokenizer's vocabulary, and roughly how big is it for modern models?
    ~32k–200k tokens
  • L1 What is BPE (byte-pair encoding)?
  • L2 How does BPE training work, step by step?
    start from bytes/chars; repeatedly merge most frequent adjacent pair
  • L2 BPE vs WordPiece vs SentencePiece/Unigram: which models use which?
  • L2 Why does the same sentence cost more tokens in Hindi or Telugu than in English?
    tokenizer trained mostly on English; more pieces per word
  • L2 What are special tokens (BOS, EOS, PAD, chat-template role markers)?
  • L2 What is a chat template, and what breaks if you apply the wrong one to an open model?
  • L2 Why are LLMs bad at counting letters ("how many r's in strawberry") and reversing words?
  • L2 Why do LLMs make arithmetic mistakes with long numbers?
    numbers split into odd token chunks
  • L2 Why does leading whitespace change the token (" hello" vs "hello")?
  • L2 How do you count tokens in Python before sending a request?
    tiktoken or the provider's count-tokens endpoint
  • L2 Why is token count, not character count, what you budget and pay for?
  • L2 What happens to code, JSON and URLs under tokenization, and why does it matter for cost?
  • L3 What is byte-level BPE, and why does it never hit "unknown token"?

Learn: HOL ch3 "Inside the Transformer Block" (pdf p107–117) · AIE ch2 "Model Architecture" (pdf p82–90) · jalammar.github.io/illustrated-transformer/ · arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762 (section 3.2)

  • L2 Why divide by √d_k?

25. RAG — retrieval-augmented generation

open this topic alone → · 329 questions

25.1 Why RAG — the pipeline end to end

Learn: AIE ch6 "RAG" (pdf p277–280) + "RAG Architecture" (pdf p280) · LEH ch4 "Why use RAG?" (pdf p129) + "The vanilla RAG framework" (pdf p130–136) · HOL ch8 "From Search to RAG" (pdf p272) · arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401

  • L1 What is RAG, in one sentence?
  • L1 What problems does RAG solve that a plain LLM cannot?
    fresh/private knowledge, citations, fewer hallucinations, smaller context
  • L1 Name the stages of a RAG pipeline.
    ingest, parse, chunk, embed, index; retrieve, rerank, assemble, generate, cite
  • L1 Offline (indexing) pipeline vs online (query) pipeline.
  • L1 What is a retriever? What is a generator?
  • L2 Draw a basic RAG system for a company help center. What runs at upload time and what at query time?
  • L2 What does "naive RAG" get wrong that "advanced RAG" fixes?
  • L2 What latency does each RAG stage add, roughly?
    embed ~10–50 ms, search ~10–50 ms, rerank ~50–300 ms, LLM seconds
  • L2 What is the source of truth in a RAG system: the documents, the vector DB, or both?
  • L2 When does RAG not help?
    reasoning/skill gaps, style/format tasks, questions needing whole-corpus aggregation
  • L2 RAG with frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex) vs writing it yourself: trade-offs.
  • L2 What metadata would you store with every chunk?
    doc id, source URL, title, section, dates, tenant, ACL, version, hash
  • L2 What would a search engineer criticise in a basic "embed, top-5, stuff the prompt" pipeline?
  • L3 Design RAG over 10 million documents. Walk through every component.
  • L3 Which RAG stage usually causes most wrong answers, and how do you prove it?
    retrieval; measure context recall separately from generation
  • L3 What is "RAG as a search problem", and why do search-engineering skills transfer?
  • L3 You have a week to ship RAG over internal docs. What do you build first and what do you skip?

  • L1 What is chunking, and why do we need it?

  • L2 What goes wrong with chunks that are too small? Too big?
    small: lost context; big: diluted embedding, wasted tokens
  • L2 How does a recursive character splitter work?

    embed sentences; cut where adjacent similarity drops

    by function/class via AST, keep file path and signatures
  • L2 How do you chunk tables so a row stays understandable?
    repeat header row; one row or small group per chunk
  • L2 How much overlap do you use, and what does overlap cost?
    ~10–20%; more storage and duplicate hits
  • L2 Chunk by tokens or by characters? Why does it matter?
  • L2 What is contextual chunk headers / contextual retrieval?
    prepend doc title or LLM-written context to each chunk before embedding
  • L2 Web pages vs PDFs vs chat transcripts: would you use the same chunker for all three?

    multi-granularity index, parent-document, summaries per section
  • L3 What is late chunking, and how does it differ from chunk-then-embed?
  • L3 How would you run an experiment to pick chunk size and overlap?
    fixed eval set; vary one knob; compare recall@k and answer quality
  • L3 You re-chunk the corpus. What else must change (IDs, citations, caches, evals)?

25.12 Failure modes and debugging "the answer is wrong"

Learn: AIE ch4 "Step 1. Evaluate All Components in a System" (pdf p224–226) · hamel.dev/blog/posts/evals/ · AIE ch6 "Retrieval Optimization" (pdf p291–297)

  • L1 Name the common RAG failure modes.
    missing doc, bad parse, wrong chunk, ranked too low, ignored, stale, conflicting
  • L2 Your RAG gives a wrong answer. Walk me through how you debug it.

  • L2 The answer exists in a document, but retrieval never returns it. What are the possible causes?
  • L2 Retrieval returns the right chunk at rank 7, and you send top 5. What do you change?
  • L2 The right chunk is in the prompt, but the model ignores it. Why, and what do you do?
  • L2 The bot answers from an old version of a policy. What happened?

  • L2 Users ask about an acronym the docs never expand. How do you fix retrieval?
  • L2 The bot answers confidently when no document is relevant. How do you fix it?
    relevance threshold, reranker cut-off, explicit refusal instruction, eval unanswerables
  • L2 Why does RAG fail on "how many" / "list all" questions over the whole corpus?
    top-k sees a sample; use SQL/aggregation or map-reduce
  • L2 What tooling would you build so anyone can see why a RAG answer was wrong?
    trace query, rewrites, retrieved ids, scores, final prompt
  • L3 Quality dropped after you upgraded the embedding model. What went wrong?

  • L3 Answers are great in English and poor in Hindi. Diagnose.
  • L3 Two near-duplicate docs keep filling the top-k with the same content. Fix it.
  • L3 A table question gets a wrong number. Which stage most likely broke?

  • L3 How do you turn every "thumbs down" into an eval case and a root-cause category?

26. AI agents and agent harnesses

open this topic alone → · 640 questions

26.1 What is an agent — agents vs workflows vs chatbots

Learn: anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents · AIE ch6 "Agent Overview" (pdf p300–302) · AIE ch10 "Step 5. Add Agent Patterns" (pdf p487–489) · Lilian Weng, "LLM Powered Autonomous Agents" (lilianweng.github.io/posts/2023-06-23-agent/) · OpenAI, "A practical guide to building agents" (openai.com/business/guides-and-resources/)

  • L1 What is an AI agent, in one sentence?
    LLM using tools in a loop, deciding its own next step, until done
  • L1 What is the difference between a chatbot, a workflow and an agent?
  • L1 Anthropic splits "agentic systems" into workflows and agents. What is the difference?
    predefined code paths vs model directs its own process and tool use
  • L1 What are the building blocks of an agent?
    model, tools, loop, state/memory, instructions, stop condition
  • L1 What is an "augmented LLM"?
  • L1 Name the five workflow patterns from "Building effective agents".
  • L2 Explain prompt chaining. When is it the right pattern? Where do you put "gates"?
  • L2 Explain routing. Give an example where a cheap router model sends easy questions to a small model.
  • L2 Explain parallelization: sectioning vs voting. Give one real use of each.
  • L2 Explain orchestrator–workers. How is it different from parallelization?
    subtasks are decided at runtime, not fixed in code
  • L2 Explain evaluator–optimizer. When does it pay off and when does it just burn tokens?
  • L2 When do you need a real agent instead of a workflow?
    open-ended steps, unpredictable path, can't hardcode the sequence
  • L2 When should you not build an agent?
    fixed steps, low error tolerance, latency/cost tight, one LLM call suffices
  • L2 What do agents trade for their flexibility?
    latency, cost, compounding errors, harder to test and debug
  • L2 What does "autonomy level" mean for an agent? Give a ladder from copilot to fully autonomous.
  • L2 Why does Anthropic say "start with the simplest solution and add complexity only when needed"? Give an example.
  • L2 A product manager says "let's make it agentic". What questions do you ask first?
  • L2 What kinds of tasks are agents good at today, and which are they bad at?
  • L2 What is the difference between an agent and an "assistant with tools" like ChatGPT with browsing?
  • L3 If each step is 95% reliable, how reliable is a 20-step agent run? What does that tell you about design?
    0.95^20 ≈ 36%; shorten paths, add verification, recover from errors
  • L3 What makes a task "agent-shaped"? Give a checklist you would use.
    clear success check, tools exist, errors recoverable, value justifies cost
  • L3 How would you turn a working agent back into a workflow once you see the common paths in traces?
  • L3 Why do frameworks sometimes make agents worse? What does "understand the underlying code" mean in practice?
  • L3 "12-factor agents" says most good agents are mostly deterministic code with LLM steps. Do you agree? Defend it.
  • L3 Is a coding agent like Claude Code a workflow or an agent? Where are the hard-coded parts?
  • L3 Which of the five patterns did you use at AiRA, and where?
    e.g. pre-LLM gate = routing, activity planner = evaluator–optimizer

26.2 The agent loop in detail

Learn: docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview · docs.anthropic.com/en/api/messages (stop_reason) · platform.openai.com/docs/guides/function-calling · AIE ch6 "Planning" (pdf p305–310) · HOL ch7 "Agents: Creating a System of LLMs" (pdf p240–245)

  • L1 Walk me through one tool call end to end.
    schemas sent → tool_use block → you execute → tool_result → model continues
  • L1 Who executes a tool: the model or your code?
  • L1 What is a tool_use block and what is a tool_result block in the Anthropic API?
  • L1 In the OpenAI Chat Completions API, how does a tool call come back and how do you send the result?
    tool_calls on assistant message; role: tool with tool_call_id
  • L1 What are the common stop reasons?
    end_turn, tool_use, max_tokens, stop_sequence, pause_turn, refusal
  • L1 Write the basic agent loop in pseudocode.
  • L1 What is "max turns" / "max steps" and why must every loop have one?
  • L2 Why must every tool_use id get a matching tool_result? What error do you get if one is missing?
  • L2 How do you report a tool failure back to the model?
    tool_result with is_error: true and a useful message, not an exception
  • L2 What are all the ways an agent loop should terminate?
    final answer, max steps, budget, timeout, cancel, fatal error, needs human
  • L2 The model stops with max_tokens in the middle of a tool call. What do you do?
  • L2 What is tool_choice and what are its options (auto / any or required / a specific tool / none)? When do you force one?
  • L2 What are parallel tool calls? How do you execute them, and how must the results be ordered and returned?
  • L2 When should you disable parallel tool calls?
    dependent writes, rate-limited APIs, order-sensitive side effects
  • L2 How do streaming tool calls work? How do you assemble partial JSON arguments from deltas?
  • L2 Can you start executing a tool before its arguments finish streaming? When is that worth it?
  • L2 Where does the model's "thinking" or reasoning go in the message history between tool calls, and must you send it back?
  • L2 How do you show progress to the user while the loop runs several tool steps?
  • L2 How does the user's message mid-run (a "steer" or interrupt) get into the loop?
  • L2 What is a server-side tool (web search, code execution run by the provider) vs a client-side tool you run?
  • L3 Two parallel tool calls: one succeeds, one times out. What do you send back?
  • L3 How do you cancel an agent run cleanly while a tool is executing? What state do you leave behind?
    cancel token, await tool cleanup, write synthetic tool_result, persist status
  • L3 The message history grows with every step. What is the cost curve of a naive loop over N steps?
    quadratic total input tokens without caching or compaction
  • L3 How would you design the loop so it can be paused and resumed on another machine?
  • L3 What is the "pause_turn" stop reason for, and how do you continue?
    long server-tool turn paused; resend to let it continue
  • L3 How do you handle a model that answers in plain text when you required a tool call (or vice versa)?
  • L3 Design the event protocol you stream to a client for an agent run (text deltas, tool start/end, approvals, errors, done).
  • L3 At AiRA you raised the loop budget to 20 steps. How did you pick that number, and what happens at step 21?

26.3 Tool design

Learn: anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents · anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents (appendix "Prompt engineering your tools") · AIE ch6 "Tools" (pdf p302–305) + "Tool selection" (pdf p319) · docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool

  • L1 What three things define a tool for an LLM?
    name, description, input JSON schema
  • L1 What makes a good tool name and a good tool description?
  • L1 What is the difference between a read tool and a write tool? Why does it matter?
  • L1 Why should tools be idempotent where possible?
  • L2 How do you design tools so the model uses them correctly?
  • L2 Should a tool be a thin wrapper around one API endpoint? Why not?
    design for agent tasks; consolidate steps; e.g. schedule_event not list+create
  • L2 How many parameters should a tool have? What do you do with optional ones?
  • L2 What should a tool return: raw JSON from the API, or something else?
    only what the model needs, readable ids, concise vs detailed modes
  • L2 A tool returns 50k tokens of output. What do you do?
    truncate, paginate, filter, summarize, write to file and return a handle
  • L2 How do you design pagination for an LLM tool?
    cursor, small default page, total count, hint how to get more
  • L2 What should a tool error message look like? Give a bad one and a good one.
    say what failed and how to fix the call
  • L2 Why return UUIDs vs human-readable names? What confuses models?
    cryptic ids cause hallucinated ids; map to names or short handles
